source.title: Efficient Self-supervised Learning with Contextualized Target Representations for Vision, Speech and Language
source.authors: Alexei Baevski; Arun Babu; Wei-Ning Hsu; M. Auli

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures downstream ImageNet accuracy across pretraining-data amounts, a different measure and setting from the claim’s scaling-law fits. It does not fit power laws or test extrapolation.
record.gate_note: Appendix B Figure 4 reports ImageNet fine-tuning accuracy after pretraining data subsets, and the text says more pretraining data helps larger models more. This bears on V6’s downstream-performance-with-scale component, but does not test loss scaling or make predictions from smaller runs. Other image, speech and language accuracy comparisons are efficiency or method comparisons, not scaling-law tests. The mention of Hoffmann et al. is background citation.
record.test_reason: This is a method-efficiency paper on data2vec 2.0. It cites Hoffmann et al. only as background. Its one scale-related result is Appendix B Figure 4: fine-tuned ImageNet top-1 accuracy for ViT-B and ViT-L after pre-training on 1–100% of ImageNet-1K. It fits no power law, reports no loss, makes no prediction from small runs, and gives no numbers. A monotone accuracy rise across seven data fractions cannot show whether downstream performance improves predictably (V6) or follows a power-law form (V5). The result is recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a test.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that data2vec 2.0 reaches the accuracy of popular existing methods in 2–16x less pre-training time across vision, speech and language, with no loss in downstream accuracy. The only scale-related statement is in Appendix B: more pretraining data helps larger models more, implying base models underfit ImageNet-1K. They draw no scaling-law conclusions.
record.recipe_differences: Measures downstream image accuracy across pretraining-data fractions; it does not fit or test the original scaling-law method, loss curves, or compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effect is considered separately for ViT-B and ViT-L; the text says larger models benefit more from increasing pretraining data.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuned ImageNet-1K top-1 accuracy rises as the self-supervised pretraining-data fraction grows from 1% to 100%. ViT-L gains more than ViT-B, which the authors read as base models underfitting the data (Appendix B, Fig. 4; figure only, no numbers).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In self-supervised vision pretraining, downstream accuracy increases monotonically with pretraining data, and larger models benefit more from extra data.

record.problems: The relevant result is shown only as a figure, with no numerical values or uncertainty estimates in the text. It covers two vision model sizes and downstream ImageNet accuracy, not language-model held-out loss or predictive extrapolation.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported image, speech and GLUE performance results compare methods and training efficiency rather than testing downstream performance as a function of scale; excluded under the gate rules.

untested.parts: All of it; no pretraining loss is reported.
All of it; no extrapolation from fitted laws.
All of it; no compute-optimal allocation.
All of it; no shape sweep at fixed parameter count.
Power-law form in vision or speech self-supervised pretraining; data scaling is shown only as an unfitted accuracy curve.
Predictability of downstream performance from scale or loss; no fit or prediction is made.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T2 / V6 'supports' verdict is overturned. V6 claims predictable improvement, and an unfitted seven-point accuracy curve for two model sizes cannot test predictability. The other results (batch size × multi-mask, epochs, method comparisons) are efficiency or ablation comparisons, not scaling tests, and were correctly left out. The Hoffmann et al. citation is background only.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model loss as a function of parameters, tokens or compute; power-law behavior and bottleneck conditions.
Prediction of much larger runs using power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its growth with compute.
Effects of depth, width and other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Whether the same power-law form holds in other modalities or training regimes.

Language-model downstream performance, predictions from pretraining loss, and prediction of downstream performance from smaller-scale runs; the reported result is limited to ImageNet accuracy versus pretraining-data amount.
Dependence of scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocations on setup or fitting choices, and departures from single power laws.

rows.subject: data2vec 2.0 ViT-B
rows.stage_stated: self-supervised pre-training on ImageNet-1K subsets, then fine-tuning on the entire ImageNet-1K
rows.operation_detail: Varied the fraction of ImageNet-1K pretraining data while keeping hyperparameters and fine-tuning data constant; reported fine-tuned top-1 accuracy.
rows.note: The authors state that increasing pretraining data helps larger models more; no numerical values for this curve are given in the text.
rows.check: The row has a figure-only value and no baseline or fit. Accuracy rising with the pretraining-data fraction (ViT-B, ImageNet-1K subsets) does not show predictability or a power-law form, so it does not measure what V6 or V5 name. The record's 'observed' state is not supportable for any version.

rows.stage_stated: self-supervised pre-training on ImageNet-1K subsets, then fine-tuning on the entire ImageNet-1K
rows.operation_detail: Varied the fraction of ImageNet-1K pretraining data while keeping hyperparameters and fine-tuning data constant; reported fine-tuned top-1 accuracy.

rows.check: Same as r1, for ViT-L. The authors' remark that larger models benefit more from data is a model-size × data interaction, not a predictability test.
